builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Spatially local mini-batching for implicit neural representations
summary: It replaces generic INRs trained on domain-wide random mini-batches with low-rank neural representations (shared basis matrices plus a small hypernetwork emitting per-layer coefficients) trained on spatially local mini-batches drawn from single AMR cells and time snapshots. The cost is the added hypernetwork and low-rank factorization machinery and a batching scheme tied to mesh refinement structure, with roughly a tenth the parameters of a comparably wide dense network; per the Kolmogorov-width argument, locality is safe because per-cell hidden states lie near a low-dimensional subspace. It can fail when the data do not come from an adaptive-mesh numerical solver, when the solution's local structure is not effectively low-rank, or when the target problem is not a PDE surrogate task, since all evidence is confined to six hyperbolic conservation laws.
rationale: The method is small-scale and GPU-friendly, but its demonstrated gains are specific to INR surrogates for adaptive-mesh PDE solutions, so it merits adoption only after validation on the reader's own scientific-ML workload.
technique: Spatially local mini-batch training of low-rank INRs

claims.statement: It replaces generic INRs trained on domain-wide random mini-batches with low-rank neural representations (shared basis matrices plus a small hypernetwork emitting per-layer coefficients) trained on spatially local mini-batches drawn from single AMR cells and time snapshots. The cost is the added hypernetwork and low-rank factorization machinery and a batching scheme tied to mesh refinement structure, with roughly a tenth the parameters of a comparably wide dense network; per the Kolmogorov-width argument, locality is safe because per-cell hidden states lie near a low-dimensional subspace. It can fail when the data do not come from an adaptive-mesh numerical solver, when the solution's local structure is not effectively low-rank, or when the target problem is not a PDE surrogate task, since all evidence is confined to six hyperbolic conservation laws.

LRNRs trained with spatially local mini-batches reach 1.1-2.3% relative L2 error on six hyperbolic conservation-law problems with one tenth of the parameters of a dense network of the same width; same-size hypernetwork-SIREN, DeepONet, and FNO baselines reach 16-78% where the LRNR reaches 4.9%.
